minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Property Owners Task Force Committee
  Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, July 9, 2024
  9:30 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  July 9, 2024 / 9:30 AM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember Craig Corman, Community
  Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis, Director of Community Development
  Michael Forbes, Director of Public Works Shana Epstein, Community
  Development Senior Planner Chloe Chen, Beverly Hills Chamber of
  Commerce President and CEO Todd Johnson, Beverly Hills Chamber of
  Commerce Director of Economic Development & Government Affairs
  Brittany Ganson, Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce Economic
  Development Manager Joseph Campbell

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Welcome & Introductions:
  a. Dar Mahbouti: Property Owner
  b. Alex Lahijani: Property Owner
  c. David Sayah: Property Owner
  d. Ming Shin Ku: Property Owner
  e. Pouya Abdi: Future Property Owner
  f. Yas Baravarian: Property Owner
  g. Kathryn Schloessman: President and CEO of the Los Angeles Sports and
  Entertainment Commission

  3) Los Angeles Sports & Entertainment Commission presentation on upcoming
  Sports and Entertainment Events:
  a. Presentation by Kathryn Schloessman:
  i. There are several high profile events coming to LA County in the next
  couple of years such as the NBA All-Star Game in 2026, the US Women’s
  Open in 2026, the FIFA World Cup in 2026, Super Bowl LXI in 2027, the
  Olympics in 2028, and the US Open Championship in 2028.
  ii. Los Angeles will be hosting 8 matches during the World Cup.
 Highlights for July 9, 2024
Property Owners Task Force Committee

  iii. Super Bowl LVI generated $477 million for the Los Angeles Region and the
  US Open Championship generated $187 million.
  iv. The World Cup is projected to generate $594 million for the Los Angeles
  Region.
  v. The Los Angeles Sports & Entertainment Commission created a
  public/private partnership called Champion LA to fund the host committees
  for these various events.
  b. Anyone who has questions about the LASEC’s Business Connect program can
  direct questions to Kathryn Schloessman.

  4) Update to Retail Queuing:
  a. Presentation by Chloe Chen:
  i. Using a stanchion and rope to allow for queuing on sidewalks was
  temporarily permitted during the pandemic as part of OpenBH.
  ii. Businesses have expressed a desire to permanently allow this now that the
  temporary OpenBH has ended.
  iii. In response to this, City staff has developed a retail queueing process
  under BHMC §8-3-4 which allows transportation/engineering officials to
  issue encroachment permits for minor encroachments on the public right
  of way.
  iv. The draft standards for the “Retail Queueing Compliance Form” are that
  the queue needs to be singe file along the façade, only during hours of
  operation, meet certain standards for set up, location, and operation.
  v. This would only be available for businesses in the Business Triangle.
  vi. To qualify for the permit, one must submit a compliance form, have an
  encroachment agreement with the city, as well as a certificate of insurance.
  vii. The permit is issued over the counter after staff review and would be active
  for one year. The permit is eligible for renewal.
  viii. The permit fee for 1 year is $963.
  ix. The City Council authorized this at the July 2nd meeting.
  x. Staff is currently developing the application forms and the permit process.
  xi. Business owners will be notified about the permit process.
  b. City staff encourages participants to apply for the permits ahead of time.
  c. Councilmember Corman and Councilmember Mirisch supported businesses using
  electronic queueing for their stores in the July 2nd hearing.
  d. Businesses are allowed to have people line up of their own accordance on the
  sidewalk, they just are not allowed to put up barriers without a permit.
  e. The city needs to make sure that the queueing structures on the sidewalk are ADA
  compliant.

  5) Information Sharing & Discussion:
  a. Someone mentioned that the economy has been doing well and that there has
  been a lot of activity on Beverly Drive.
  b. Someone else stated that there has been a revitalization for retail space and that
  the security in Beverly Hills plays a large role in businesses deciding to move here.
 Highlights for July 9, 2024
Property Owners Task Force Committee

  He also stated that the bollards are too close together and protrude into the walking
  space of the sidewalk.
  c. A third person applauded the city’s approach to homelessness and cracking down
  on panhandling. He also noted that restaurants have had trouble opening due to
  the time and costs of getting authorization from LA County.
  d. The Maestros expansion to the penthouse should be complete in the next two
  months and should be open by the end of October.
  e. The Assistant City Manager noted that most of the time, when a property is taking
  a while to have a design approved, it is due to the architect not submitting forms in
  a timely fashion rather than the city leaving it on the backburner.

  6) Future Agenda Items Discussion:
  a. None

  7) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: June 9, 2024 / 10:26 AM
